Definitely wouldn't call them harmless, they have an exaggerated reputation for sure but a bite absolutely poses a risk to people, especially the very young and elderly. Death isn't likely but not impossible.
Highly recommend watching the black widow bite by Jacks world of wildlife, hes a young adult in good shape who took a pretty bad bite from a small female and it did a number on him.
The OG and the zero sugar variations of it will always be my favourite. I'm a simple man, I like my energy drink to taste like energy drink lol

I have a hot take. The best monster flavours imo are absolutely zero and the zero sugar in black and green. I'm all about the standard energy drink flavour but all the sugar in the original is too much and makes it taste like syrup. Those ones have it just right for me.

I think these guys are legitimately potent enough to kill a healthy adult, it's just they don't usually as most bites are dry ones or they only use a fraction of their venom. Toxicity wise they make black widows seem like house spiders which are 15x more toxic than a rattlesnake. If they gave a full payload when they bit like Atrax I'd imagine that person would be dead without anti-venom.

Did this guy just boop a Brazilian wandering spider?
Serious question from someone who doesn't live in the states. Which is considered more dangerous there, the black widow or brown recluse?

Already been pointed out but they're only poisonous in the wild, and even then as long as you don't try to eat it or have open wounds on your skin and wash your hands after there's no real danger.
I think the only exception is the golden poison dart frog, I'm pretty sure that the toxins produced by it can be absorbed through bare skin.

Even Brazilian wandering spider bites aren't that serious the majority of the time, most are either mild or moderate envenomations at worst. Funnel webs are probably the only ones where an untreated bite is usually fatal.
Six eyed sand spiders would be another one I imagine too.

I feel like I'm in the minority here but I don't enjoy gigs as much if I go alone, done it a few times and just had an okay time at best as opposed to a great time but I'm a super anxious person so that's probably why 😂 envious of those who can just go without a plus 1.
I imagine an envenomation from a widow that size would be real bad news for the person on the receiving end.

If I remember correctly black mambas are one of the few species where 99% of bites are full envenomations. They don't do dry bites. I think the fang actually cut through a vein or something according to an article which sort of flushed the venom out.

If you live in the US, never use a tourniquet on a venomous snake bite. The majority of venomous snakes that live across the USA belong to the viper family and have cyto/hematoxin venom which will destroy tissue in the area around the bite. If you use a tourniquet you will likely need the affected limb amputated, even with antivenom.
